title: Physical absorption audit: a generic row loss and its parity repair
analyticClaims: For the all-odd Rudin-Shapiro family with a=1 and delta=M, the generic B_A term in the R0.72H corollary is not individually absorbed by the candidate physical payment.
Odd carriers make V exchange even and odd lattice parity, so P0 V^2 F depends only on the smaller even component.
In the perturbative all-odd regime, the physical normalized root ledger is governed by R(M,g)=g^(4/3) M^(-2)/(1+q^2 g^2 M^(-1) Psi(M^2 X)); on a bounded physical window its optimized envelope decays.
finiteDiagnostics: The producer uses delta=M on M=4,8,16,32,64,128 and measures the cubic exposure rather than substituting its generic B_A Q_* upper bound.
If an independent data file is present at build time, matching finite values are overlaid with open-square markers.
The exact-root curve is one certified atom and the measured BV curve is an upper ledger assembled from continuous integrals; neither is a numerical enumeration of every root.
claimBoundary: The parity conclusion and scaling audit are confined to the all-odd compatible-real finite-carrier triangular 2.5D family. The growing generic B_A bound diagnoses a lossy factorization, not a growing physical Navier-Stokes root ledger. This figure does not prove a continuation criterion, blow-up, or general three-dimensional Navier-Stokes regularity.
